item.title: How UK dual nationals in Europe can renounce British citizenship
item.description: If you wish to give up British citizenship - here's how to do it, how much it costs and how, in some cases, you can get it back.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Thursday
item.description: Migration minister 'working on solution' for teen deportations, police unable to warn free schools if teachers are suspected and more news from Sweden on Thursday.

item.title: 'If I’d known, I wouldn't have come': How Sweden's teen deportations deter skilled workers
item.description: They study at some of Sweden's top universities and their parents hold senior positions at companies like Tetra Pak, Ericsson, and Volvo Cars. The Local has heard from more than 50 people affected by the teen deportation issue.

item.title: What we know about Sweden’s new self-sufficiency requirement for citizenship
item.description: Sweden’s government has revealed more details about its plans to tighten up citizenship rules, including introducing a self-sufficiency requirement for citizenship applicants. Here’s what we know so far.

item.title: Man faces trial in Sweden for leaving 'Hitler apples' at migration minister's house
item.description: A man who left apples painted with features resembling Adolf Hitler outside Migration Minister Johan Forssell’s house is to go on trial for illegal protest and making an aggravated threat.

item.title: EXPLAINED: How to avoid Sweden's teen deportation trap
item.description: Teen deportations are now a political issue in Sweden after increased reporting in Swedish-language media. The migration team at EY explained the problem to The Local and how to avoid it.

item.title: Do skiers and snowboarders have to wear helmets on Swedish slopes?
item.description: As Swedish ski resorts fill up with February ski tourists, The Local looks at the regulations for skiers in Sweden.

item.title: Why have thousands of furries taken over central Malmö?
item.description: If you've been in Malmö over the past few days you've almost certainly noticed them ‒ thousands of people dressed up in colourful animal costumes have suddenly appeared in the city. But who are they and why are they here?

item.title: Swedish word of the day: snus
item.description: There are fewer things more Swedish than snus, the small nicotine pouches wedged under the lips of one in seven Swedes. But where does the word snus actually come from?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Friday
item.description: Sweden Democrat leader willing to delay PR revocation law, Sweden to develop air raid warning app, government unveils new prison conditions for teens and more news from Sweden on Friday.
